Camille Ortiz: Proposal: run a behavior-driven weekly digest for active devs — dynamic sections based on product usage (embeddings, chat, inference). Keep it to 3 tiles + 1 CTA. Goal: drive to benchmark page or start a sandbox. Thoughts?
Diego Morales: Love it. For dynamic content we should use merge keys: {{usage_segment}}, {{top_feature}}, {{cta_label}}. Keep fallback content for unknowns.
Harper Nguyen: Segmentation idea: Active (>=3 API calls last 7d), Lurkers (signed up but <3 calls), New (signed up last 48h). Each gets different hero and CTA.
Mina Patel: Subject line test: A) "Your weekly Redwood digest: tips for {{top_feature}}" B) "See how teams cut cost on inference". Run subject A on Active, B on Lurkers.
Camille Ortiz: Content tiles: 1) Quick tip (1-sentence + code snip), 2) Benchmark highlight (stat + link), 3) Customer snippet (1 line). CTA: Active -> sandbox, Lurkers -> 1-click quickstart, New -> watch 3-min demo.
Diego Morales: For code snippet include single-line shell or curl examples. Example: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY'`
Harper Nguyen: Tracking: utm_campaign=weekly_dynamic, utm_content=tile1|tile2|tile3, and include header X-User-Segment in tracking webhook for downstream analytics.
Mina Patel: Deliverability checks: avoid >2 images, inline critical copy, make plain-text version obvious. Also warm-send for new segment: 200/day ramp for first week.
Camille Ortiz: Ops checklist:
```
- Build 3 modular blocks in template builder
- Add merge key tests on staging data (50 rows)
- Create segment exports: active, lurker, new
- Set subject-line A/B and winner threshold (open delta >4%)
- Schedule warm ramp for new segment
- Configure webhook for clicks to include segment header
```
Diego Morales: Automation note: ops-bot can handle ramping. @ops-bot please run warm ramp: 200/day -> 500/day -> full over 7 days if metrics stable.
ops-bot: Warm ramp workflow queued. Stage send scheduled: 2024-06-10 08:00 PT to staging-list. Ramp plan attached to campaign.
Harper Nguyen: Quick QA: make sure merge keys are present or template falls back to neutral copy: "Explore Redwood". Also test in inbox preview for gmail/outlook.
Mina Patel: Can we include a tiny poll (1-click) in footer: "Which feature matters most? [Cost][Latency][Privacy]" Use trackable links to update segment membership.
Camille Ortiz: Yes — great idea. That'll help refine dynamic logic. Next steps: Diego implements merge keys + webhook, Harper builds template and QA, Mina sets ramp and poll links. We'll dry run to 100 internal on Monday then ramp. :rocket:
